title: Modal logic and formal metaphysics
audience: a college student in a philosophy degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn modal logic and its uses in metaphysics: the language of necessity and possibility, Kripke models and frames, the systems K, T, S4 and S5 and their frame conditions, proofs and countermodels, quantified modal logic with varying domains and the Barcan formula, counterfactuals in Lewis-Stalnaker semantics, temporal and deontic logic, and formalized arguments in metaphysics, with Python model checkers.
primary_reading: Boxes and Diamonds: an open introduction to modal logic (Open Logic Project, free)

weeks.1: The modal language: necessity, possibility and duality
weeks.2: Kripke models: worlds, accessibility and truth
weeks.3: Validity in frames and the system K
weeks.4: Frame conditions: reflexive, transitive, symmetric and Euclidean
weeks.5: The systems T, S4 and S5
weeks.7: Countermodels and the finite model property
weeks.8: Quantified modal logic: domains and the Barcan formula
weeks.11: Formal metaphysics: the modal ontological argument
weeks.12: Necessitism, contingentism and the logic of existence

blocks.deliverable: Evaluate ten formulas in a Kripke model by hand and in Python.
Prove which axioms each frame condition validates.
Prove five theorems in S4 and S5.
Week 7 midterm; build countermodels for five invalid formulas.
Evaluate counterfactuals in a model with a similarity ordering.
Formalize a modal argument and test it in S5.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Modal model checker: write and test a Python program that represents Kripke models, evaluates propositional modal formulas, checks frame conditions and tests formulas for validity on all frames up to a small size, then use it to analyze one modal argument from metaphysics and write a two-page report on what you found.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
